id: title:Gilbert09:accept a pasted project url in the project field

observations.behavior: Adds normalize_project_ref to strip protocol and sub-path from URLs before encoding.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows warehouse import configuration to accept full GitLab URLs while still reaching the correct project endpoint.

observations.behavior: Replaces manual stripping and digit checks with normalized input; unifies error message when path segments are missing or empty.
observations.posthog_connection: Reduces false negatives where users paste complete URLs but receive token-related errors instead of clear guidance on required group/project ID or path.

observations.behavior: Adds tests asserting that pasted URLs resolve correctly without failing early validation, including trailing .git and issue paths stripped away.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection against regressions introduced by URL normalization and ensures compatibility across common user inputs.

observations.limitations: Only backend connector and its unit tests are shown; no runtime behavior, integration results, or production metrics. No change to shared middleware, database migrations, or broader orchestration is visible.

review.limitations: Only backend connector and its unit tests are shown; no runtime behavior, integration results, or production metrics. No change to shared middleware, database migrations, or broader orchestration is visible.
review.reason: The implementation demonstrates a bounded correctness improvement in warehouse ingestion: it normalizes diverse user inputs into valid API requests and removes an avoidable class of 404s caused by malformed encoding. Tests cover representative cases. This does not reach tier 3 because the benefit remains localized to this connector rather than systemic risk reduction across PostHog’s critical paths.
review.posthog_relevance: Helps warehouse import configuration reliability for GitLab-backed warehouses; reduces support burden from misconfigured project references.
review.uncertainty: Assessment relies solely on supplied hunks; adoption and actual incident avoidance cannot be established.
